title: Completed-module section reindexing and its reverse
statement: For every adic coefficient datum d over a commutative ring A in Type(t+1), schemes T,T prime in Scheme(t), and scheme isomorphism u:T prime -> T, the published completed-ring tensor pullback has a natural underlying abelian-sheaf identification with sectionwise inverse-image reindexing. Its inverse on a local section x over the postcomposed test is the inverse-image unit applied to x followed by restriction along proEtaleIsoCommaArrow. There is an equivalence between the completed-ring module categories whose forward functor equals the published tensor pullback along u and whose inverse equals the published tensor pullback along inv u. This is an assertion about ordinary completed-ring modules only; it asserts no tower, derived-limit, reduction, or exchange compatibility. The coefficient datum and the concrete canonical maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and [def-pur-completed-reindexing-data].

proof.text: Use the covering-preserving site equivalence and its comma-normalized inverse-image identification. Transport each module action by the inverse completed coefficient identification. The coefficient composition equation identifies reverse transport with the coefficient comparison for inv u.

The published tensor pullback is left adjoint to the sectionwise direct image with this coefficient action. Its tensor-unit-normalized adjunction identifies it with the action-transport functor. Under this identification its inverse-image unit is the comma coprojection, so the inverse identification is the displayed unit followed by restriction. The coefficient identity and composition equations provide the natural unit and counit and identify the inverse functor with the reverse published tensor pullback.
